# Target (5 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /product | `tcin` | 5 | Get a Target product by TCIN |
| /reviews | `tcin` | 5 | Get Target product reviews |
| /category | `category_id` | 5 | Browse Target products in a category |
| /categories | *(none)* | 1 | List the Target category taxonomy |
| /stores | `query` | 1 | Find Target stores near a location |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /product — 5cr

Returns full product detail for a Target item: title, brand, description, highlight bullets, current and regular price, average rating with its 1-5 star distribution, written-review count, the full image gallery, colour and size variations, and stock status. Prices are national: Target's product endpoint reports the same price whatever store is asked for, so treat this as catalogue pricing rather than shelf pricing. For this product's written reviews call GET /v1/target/reviews with the same TCIN.

**Parameters**

- `tcin`: Target catalogue id (TCIN), the numeric id at the end of a target.com product URL: target.com/p/<name>/-/A-92148487 is TCIN 92148487. Target rolls a colour or size variant up to its parent product, so the id returned by GET /v1/target/product can differ from the one you sent; the id you asked for is preserved at product.ext.requested_id.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/target/product?tcin=<tcin>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /reviews — 5cr

Returns written customer reviews for a Target product, 10 per page, each with the full review text, star rating, reviewer nickname, submission date, helpful-vote count, verified-purchase flag, and any reviewer photos. Pages do not overlap and the review total is exact, so a full crawl is deterministic: pass the returned cursor back until has_more is false. Page size is fixed by the upstream at 10 and cannot be raised. If you want the star distribution rather than the review text, call GET /v1/target/product instead and read product.ext.rating_distribution, which is one call rather than one per ten reviews.

**Parameters**

- `tcin`: Target catalogue id (TCIN), the numeric id at the end of a target.com product URL: target.com/p/<name>/-/A-92148487 is TCIN 92148487. Target rolls a colour or size variant up to its parent product, so the id returned by GET /v1/target/product can differ from the one you sent; the id you asked for is preserved at product.ext.requested_id.
- `page` *(optional)*: Page number, starting at 1. Prefer the universal cursor parameter. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/target/reviews?tcin=<tcin>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /category — 5cr

Returns products listed in a Target category, 24 per page, each with title, brand, price, regular price, rating, image gallery, highlight bullets, and its TCIN. Unlike Target's keyword search this one paginates, so it is the way to walk a whole category: pass the returned cursor back until has_more is false. Because Target ships no keyword search worth billing for, this plus GET /v1/target/categories is how you discover TCINs. Two things to expect: consecutive pages occasionally repeat a handful of products, because Target's category ordering shifts between calls, so de-duplicate by product.id when crawling; and ratings are present on roughly half of category rows and null on the rest, which reflects Target's own data rather than an omission here.

**Parameters**

- `category_id`: Target category node id, for example hz89j for Kitchen & Dining. Ids come from GET /v1/target/categories, and also appear in the category URLs on target.com (/c/<name>/-/N-<id>).
- `page` *(optional)*: Page number, starting at 1. Prefer the universal cursor parameter. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/target/category?category_id=<category_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /categories — 1cr

Returns Target's top-level browse taxonomy: each node's id, display name, parent id, canonical URL, and hero image. Feed a node id into GET /v1/target/category to walk that category's products. This is the entry point for TCIN discovery, since Target ships no keyword search we are willing to bill for. Static reference data, so it is 1 credit and heavily cached.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/target/categories" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /stores — 1cr

Returns Target stores near a ZIP code, city, or state, each with its store id, name, full address, phone number, distance from the searched location, open/closed status, timezone, and two weeks of daily opening hours. Store data changes rarely, so it is 1 credit and heavily cached. Note that Target's product pricing is national on this API, so a store id here is for store-locator use rather than for localising prices.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Location to search near: a ZIP code (10001), a city (Austin), or a state. Both ZIP and city forms are verified.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/target/stores?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a Target endpoint

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| One product's detail (by TCIN) | `/product` | 5 |
| What buyers say | `/reviews` | 5 |
| Browse a category | `/category` | 5 |
| The category taxonomy | `/categories` | 1 |
| Stores near a location | `/stores` | 1 |

### Spend the 1cr calls first

`/categories` (1cr) returns the taxonomy — call it before `/category` (5cr) so you browse a
category that actually exists. `/stores` (1cr) is the only local-availability signal here.

Note there is **no keyword search** on Target: you need a TCIN (Target's item id) for
`/product`, or you browse in via `/category`. If all you have is a product name, find the TCIN
elsewhere first — `google_shopping/product-search` (5cr) or `web/search` (2cr) will surface
the Target listing URL.
